nodes.name: Computational Coordination Design
nodes.procedure: In line with our strategy, substituting one or two nonmetal atoms (B, C, O, P and S) for N atom(s) generates five types, totally 36 new FeXY_iN_{3-i} (i = 0,1) coordinated systems (FeXN3, homogeneous double atom-doped FeXYN2-I(II) (X=Y), and heterogeneous double atom-doped FeXYN2-I(II) (X≠Y)). Formation energy calculated by E_f = E_FeXY_iN_{3-i} - (E_PP + μ_X + i μ_Y + μ_Fe) + (i+1) μ_N confirms thermodynamic stability (all E_f < 0). Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations at 500K for 5ps and dissolution potential U_diss > 0 confirm thermal and electrochemical stability.
nodes.source_text: Figure 1a... substituting one or two nonmetal atoms (B, C, O, P and S) for N atom(s) generates five types, totally 36 new FeXY_iN_{3-i} (i = 0,1) coordinated systems, Figure 1b and Tables S1-S3... formation energies for all systems considered here are well below zero... AIMD simulations at 500K for 5 ps.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations at 500 K for 5 ps show structures remain stable without significant distortion for all FeXY_iN_{3-i} systems.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the stability of these systems is further evaluated by ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations at a high enough temperature of 500K for 5 ps... indicative of high thermal stability under ambient conditions.

nodes.characterization_summary: Dissolution potentials for all systems are well above zero, indicating desirable electrochemical stability in acidic environments.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It can be seen that all of them are well above zero, indicative of the desirable durability of these FeXY_iN_{3-i} structures in acidic environments.

nodes.characterization_summary: All FeXY_iN_{3-i} coordinated systems exhibit superior metallic conductivity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: one can find that all of them are featured with superior metallic conductivity.

nodes.characterization_summary: Projected density of states confirms Fe 3d orbital occupancy changes in FeC₂N₂-II with b_{2g} orbital half occupied due to symmetry breaking.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure 4c, projected density of states (PDOS) confirms the occupancy of Fe 3d orbitals.

nodes.characterization_summary: COHP analysis shows *O-FeC₂N₂-II bond order BO=1.5 (vs BO=2 for FeN₄), reducing *O adsorption strength and yielding η^OER=0.17 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: *O bonding to FeC₂N₂-II complex leads to a smaller bond order (BO = 1.5)... accounting for the lowered *O adsorption strength and the significantly low overpotential (0.17 V).

nodes.characterization_summary: HER activity assessed by ΔG_*H values; seven systems show |ΔG_*H| ≤ 0.1 eV including FePN₃ (-0.06 eV), FeOPN₂-I (0.04 eV), FeC₂N₂-II (-0.07 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: ΔG_*H of FePN₃ (-0.06 eV) FeOPN₂-I (0.04 eV) FeOPN₂-II (0.06 eV) FeCON₂-II (0.03 eV) FeC₂N₂-I (0.01 eV) FeC₂N₂-II (-0.07 eV) and FeP₂N₂-I (-0.1 eV) turns out to be very close to the ideal value of zero

nodes.characterization_summary: OER overpotentials calculated; FeC₂N₂-II shows extremely low η^OER = 0.17 V, breaking standard scaling relationship.
nodes.evidence_snippet: FeC₂N₂-II has the best OER activity with the overpotential η^OER being only 0.17 V... breaking the limitation of the standard scaling relationship
